description: What a Korean exporter of this product is likely to miss in a market — the unknown unknowns beyond the product category's usual compliance: rules that can stop the sale (e.g. UV filters not allowed in US sunscreen, meat ingredients from countries the EU has not listed), approvals needed before import or sale (radio certification such as FCC, EU RED, Japan's Giteki or Canada's ISED; India BIS; registration of special-use cosmetics in China), extra duties or charges that change the quote (US Section 232 on steel and aluminium content, EU CBAM), and filings or labels (EU deforestation due diligence, producer registration (EPR) for batteries and electronics, and packaging EPR such as Germany's LUCID register in packaging_epr, EU ban on generic green claims), plus Korea-side checks (strategic items, dangerous goods in shipping). Each rule is triggered by the exact HS code or a product trait (pass description or traits) and comes with kind, gate (true = clear it before anything else: the plan's before-you-sell gate), who must act (you or the importer), the date it applies from (upcoming rules too), the official source and the date it was checked; stale marks rules not re-checked for 180 days. The category compliance pointer and its official source are included per market. Each market also says how much TradeGraph knows there (rules_coverage: national, bloc, pointers or none, where none is not a clearance and how_to_check lists where to look); where it has no rule note, rule_pointers gives official-source starting points for blocs and countries such as the EAEU (Kazakhstan, Russia, Belarus, Armenia, Kyrgyzstan), the Andean Community, Mexico, Chile, Argentina, Türkiye, Egypt, Israel, South Africa, Nigeria, Kenya, Pakistan, Bangladesh, New Zealand, Uzbekistan and Mongolia, gate marking what must be met before import or sale. Omit country to check every market in the plan's table. Starting points, not legal advice. Free, read-only.

country.description: Target country as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (e.g. 'US', 'JP') or an English/Korean name. Optional: omit to check the markets of the plan's table.

description.description: Optional: the product as the user describes it, any language (e.g. '비건 선크림 SPF50', '할랄 인증 저가 립스틱', 'premium anti-aging ampoule already on Amazon US'). Used to detect product traits that change the rules within one HS code (see traits) and the concepts, price tier, certifications and markets already selling that change which market fits (product_profile, entry_paths).

item.description: Product as an HS4 code (e.g. '3304') or a name in English or Korean (e.g. 'sunscreen', '라면'). Names cover TradeGraph's 35 items; any other product works as a 4-digit HS code (e.g. '1905' biscuits, '2005' kimchi, '3305' shampoo) with live UN Comtrade imports.

product.description: Optional: the product's own name in English (e.g. 'vegan sunscreen').

traits.description: Optional: product traits, comma-separated, that change the rules within one HS code: sunscreen, whitening (also arbutin, kojic acid), vitamin_a (retinol), gel_nail (UV/LED gel, semi-cured strips), contact_lens (HS 9001: contact lenses, colour lenses), hair_dye, hair_loss, acne, antiperspirant, dandruff, fluoride (toothpaste), human_derived (human stem cell culture media, human placenta, cord blood: a ban in the EU, UK, China and ASEAN), stem_cell (stem cell culture media whose source is not named: check it), exosome, radio (Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, cellular), battery, meat, dairy, egg, aerosol, flammable, industrial or household (for HS codes that hold both, such as 8414 fans, compressors and vacuum pumps: picks machinery rules, trade fairs and buyer searches, or household-appliance ones). Also detected from item, product and description; the answer lists them in product_traits.

name: blind_spots
title: What exporters miss: blockers, approvals, extra duties
